planting.note: Plant container-grown specimens in spring in well-drained, moist to moderately dry soil in full sun; Bermuda Palmetto is the only palm species native to Bermuda and tolerates salt spray and coastal wind exceptionally well.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moist to moderately dry soil in full sun; once established, Bermuda Palmetto tolerates drought, salt spray, and coastal wind exceptionally well, reflecting its origin on the exposed, storm-battered island it's named for. It is the only palm species native to Bermuda and one of only a handful of true island-endemic palms in the Atlantic, bearing large, stiff, fan-shaped fronds on a stout trunk topped with the persistent leaf-base 'boot' pattern typical of the genus. Slow-growing and long-lived, it makes an excellent coastal landscape specimen where salt tolerance is essential, and needs little care once established beyond occasional removal of old fronds.
